prompt.context: Your client NileKart is located in the Research Triangle Park (RTP) in Durham. It is the nation's fastest growing e-commerce player with over $3 billion in revenues in 2015. Most of this growth is inorganic, with NileKart leveraging its seemingly endless cash reserves to acquire companies that strategically align with its long-term vision of becoming the largest e-commerce company in the world. NileKart's recent acquisitions include a fast-growing logistics company based in Memphis, a 600-seat call center based in Austin, and a Fintech start-up based in Silicon Valley. In January 2016, under tremendous pressure from its VCs to continue rapid growth, NileKart reluctantly completed the acquisition of WishDeal — a niche e-commerce company with over $500 million in revenues in 2015. WishDeal is based in Silicon Valley and was built by a young team of data scientists and developers; it sells quirky, one-of-a-kind products at low prices. The rationale behind this merger was to exploit economies of scale in operations, expand the consumer base, and develop a diverse product portfolio as sources of competitive advantage in the highly saturated U.S. e-commerce industry.
prompt.question: We have been engaged to help with creating a comprehensive technology integration plan. Please address the following key considerations: (1) Who are the key stakeholders that need to be considered in order to achieve success of the technology integration? (2) How would you integrate NileKart's and WishDeal's technology systems into a single centralized platform where the combined entity can leverage economies of scale in operations? (3) What phases would you propose to roll out the integration, with broad timelines? (4) What are the key risks that NileKart faces in this integration?

clarifying_info.q: Can you describe the culture at NileKart and WishDeal?
clarifying_info.a: NileKart has a collaborative and entrepreneurial culture; its leadership team is made up of seasoned industry veterans who control the majority of decision-making and most initiatives require a sign-off from the leadership team before implementation. WishDeal has an agile, entrepreneurial, and decentralized culture where product managers and business heads are given a lot of freedom to implement initiatives and run their divisions independently.

clarifying_info.q: Why was NileKart reluctant to acquire WishDeal?
clarifying_info.a: NileKart's management felt that the company cultures were very different and that rushing into a new, sizable acquisition without first consolidating its existing portfolio of acquired companies would not be beneficial in the long run.

clarifying_info.q: How has NileKart fared in its previous acquisitions?
clarifying_info.a: 80% of NileKart's acquisitions have been successful in achieving the desired objectives.

clarifying_info.q: Why is this integration important to both companies, and is the leadership team aligned?
clarifying_info.a: The rationale behind the merger was to exploit economies of scale in operations, expand the consumer base, and develop a diverse product portfolio. The leadership team at NileKart is highly committed to making this merger successful, but the leadership team at WishDeal is apprehensive about losing their agile culture and focus on selling unique, quirky products to a younger customer base.

clarifying_info.q: What are the current technology systems at both companies?
clarifying_info.a: Both companies use SAP as their ERP system. NileKart uses Salesforce.com's proprietary CRM system, while WishDeal uses Zoho CRM's SaaS CRM system. Unifying both CRMs will be a critical piece in ensuring successful integration of customer data and developing future business strategy.

clarifying_info.q: Has NileKart given any specific timelines given the influence of the VCs?
clarifying_info.a: The Board, comprising several VC partners, is hoping to successfully complete the integration of WishDeal into NileKart's operations within the next two years.

clarifying_info.q: Are both players selling similar products? What are the differences in customer base or go-to-market approach?
clarifying_info.a: NileKart sells everything from a pin to a plane on its e-commerce platform; its customer base is between the ages of 21 and 45. WishDeal focuses on selling unique, quirky items at low prices to customers typically between the ages of 16 and 28. WishDeal leverages customer data analytics to deliver targeted marketing via Instagram, Pinterest, and Snapchat. NileKart leverages traditional social media marketing.

clarifying_info.q: Who are the end users of the unified CRM?
clarifying_info.a: The end users will be the 800 employees of NileKart's Austin-based call center along with a 60-member customer support team from WishDeal. The preference is to migrate WishDeal's CRM data into the Salesforce.com CRM used by NileKart.

clarifying_info.q: Are there any change champions identified for the ERP and CRM integration project?
clarifying_info.a: Yes. The CTOs of both companies are championing the cause, along with a special task force comprising senior project managers, the technology team, and the customer satisfaction team from the Austin-based call center.

framework: Option 1 — Lifecycle framework: Present the solution as a series of next steps with appropriate detail and timelines (e.g., Gantt chart format).
Option 2 — Work Streams framework: Go deeper into all case-specific Human Capital work streams relevant to the integration.
Option 3 — People–Process–Technology framework: Divide activities by area of impact (People, Process, Technology).

Option 4 — Assess–Design–Deploy–Measure framework: Divide activities by project phase (Assess Current State, Design Future State, Deploy & Measure), with at least two work streams per phase and potential overlaps.
Regardless of framework chosen, all four questions from the prompt must be addressed: stakeholders, technology integration approach, phased rollout with timelines, and key risks.

questions.prompt: Who are the key stakeholders that need to be considered in this technology integration?
questions.guidance: A strong answer identifies stakeholders across multiple levels and entities: (1) Executive leadership teams of NileKart and WishDeal; (2) Executive leadership teams of the other acquired entities (logistics company in Memphis, call center in Austin, Fintech start-up in Silicon Valley) — to ensure seamless integration and unlock economies of scale; (3) VC partners who hold strategic interests; (4) CTOs and technology teams at both NileKart and WishDeal; (5) Employees at NileKart's Austin call center (800 employees) and WishDeal's customer support team (60 members).

questions.prompt: How would you integrate the technology systems into a single centralized platform? Walk through your approach.
questions.guidance: A strong answer addresses four dimensions: (1) Leadership Alignment — survey leaders to identify allies, pilot in supportive divisions first, have positive leaders engage skeptical ones, communicate the benefits and each leader's role and rewards; (2) Communications — tailor messaging by stakeholder group, cascade from local office leadership, communicate benefits of a unified CRM, set expectations about a learning curve and temporary productivity dip; (3) Incentives — create visible recognition programs (e.g., awards to highest-adoption office), celebrate milestones; (4) Stakeholder Engagement — identify change champions who are positive and understand the business, gather employee feedback continuously, account for cultural differences so a one-size-fits-all approach is avoided; (5) Training — redesign training to address local office business needs, grounded in a thorough understanding of current business processes and how they change with migration to Salesforce.com.

questions.prompt: What phases would you propose for the rollout, with broad timelines?
questions.guidance: Using the Assess–Design–Deploy–Measure framework as an example: Phase 1 Assess Current State — stakeholder analysis, culture and talent retention analysis, skills gap analysis, current technology/data audit, communications strategy development. Phase 2 Design Future State — identify change team, create organization structure, design training programs, develop IT strategy for CRM migration from Zoho to Salesforce.com. Phase 3 Deploy & Measure — run surveys, hold focus groups, manage resistance, create milestones, reduce headcount where needed, manage goodwill, run training programs, provide IT help desk and tech support. Overall timeline: two years per VC expectations. Candidate should acknowledge that overlapping work streams are expected.

questions.prompt: What are the key risks NileKart faces in this integration?
questions.guidance: A strong answer covers: (1) Attrition of top talent, especially in engineering and product management teams; (2) Loss of WishDeal's customer base if customers fear a decline in quality or changes in customer service standards; (3) Loss of employee morale due to differences in company cultures and leadership styles (centralized vs. decentralized); (4) Competitors moving quickly to capture market share if the integration fails or drags; (5) Loss of brand value and lower NileKart valuation resulting in potential VC losses.

recommendation: Adopt the Assess–Design–Deploy–Measure framework with People, Process, and Technology work streams to ensure all dimensions of integration are covered within the two-year VC-mandated timeline.
Prioritize CRM unification (Zoho to Salesforce.com) as the critical path item because it directly affects the 860 combined customer-facing employees and underpins the combined customer data strategy.
Begin with a pilot in divisions led by allies identified in the leadership alignment survey before rolling out company-wide.
risks: Cultural clash between NileKart's centralized decision-making and WishDeal's decentralized, agile culture could undermine adoption and morale.
Top talent attrition in engineering and product management at WishDeal if employees feel autonomy is being removed.
WishDeal's younger customer base (16–28) may disengage if the brand's quirky identity is diluted during integration.
A failed or delayed integration could invite competitors to capture market share and erode VC confidence.
next_steps: Conduct leadership alignment surveys at both companies within the first 30 days.
Form the cross-functional integration task force (CTOs + senior project managers + customer satisfaction leads) and define governance.
Commission a detailed skills gap analysis and CRM data audit in parallel.
Develop a phased communications plan tailored to each stakeholder group before any system changes are announced to employees.
